folded.object: words with tonic stress on the penultimate syllable

spans.text: The two largest stress groups are words with tonic stress on the penultimate syllable, as in kaza ‘house’, and on the final syllable, as in kumí ‘eat’.
Smaller stress groups are those words with a stressed antepenultimate syllable, such as kólera ‘cholera’, and some monosyllables such as kí ‘what?’.

folded.subject: The lexicon

spans.text: The lexicon of Papiá Kristang is principally Portuguese-derived, with a good number of Malay-based items and items from other sources, including Cantonese, Dutch, Hindi, Hokkien, Konkani and Malayalam.
The noun is invariable.
There are 18 consonants in Papiá Kristang, of which [v] occurs only in one word: novi ‘nine’ (see Table 2).
Although still being acquired by some children in Malacca, Papiá Kristang is an endangered language because of a strong generational shift towards English as the dominant language.
Subsequently, further external influence on Papiá Kristang would have occurred through connections with Asian ports where Portuguese and Creole Portuguese communities existed.
Elderly Papiá-Kristang-dominant mother-tongue speakers are few and the transmission to younger generations is very weak.
